Date: 2028-01-11 | Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Ortega (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Santella - Head Platform), Raj Kapoor (Santella CTO), Emily Nguyen (Santella Infra), Theo Marsh (Santella Procurement)
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer intends to renew with a modest uplift to capacity and activate an EU region (private VPC option). Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, private VPC vs hosted EU, SOC2/KMS integration, pilot timeline, and contract amendment path. Action items assigned for runbook, latency tests, and procurement PO. Next meeting tentatively scheduled after EU pilot baseline tests.
topics: EU region activation (private VPC vs hosted)
transcript:
00:00 Lena Ortiz: Okay I think we can start, folks. Thanks for joining.
00:07 Maya Chen: hey everyone, Maya from Redwood, thanks for making time. we pulled together the renewal notes and the EU on-boarding plan to walk through.
00:15 Raj Kapoor: morning, sorry small delay on my side. we had a quick infra stand.
00:20 Samir Patel: no worries. i'll kick off with the technical runbook in a minute. quick agenda check — renewal numbers, region options, security questions, then actions. sound good?
00:30 Lena Ortiz: yep that's good. our procurement rep Theo will chime on timing.
00:35 Theo Marsh: thanks, yes i'll listen for PO timing and any contract items.
00:41 Maya Chen: high level — Santella current committed capacity sits at 45k token units per month, usage close to 78% on peak. you've asked about a 20-30% uplift and EU activation for residency. correct?
00:54 Emily Nguyen: that's right. lots of regulatory flags in EU clinical trials data so residency is required, plus lower latency for EU customers.
01:03 Raj Kapoor: and we want to keep an eye on per-token cost; latency on the read path is important for our triage UI.
01:10 Samir Patel: got it. so two distinct options: hosted EU (Redwood-managed infra in eu-west) which is fastest to activate, or private VPC in EU where you control network and KMS keys. tradeoffs are latency, control, and cost. private VPC adds a bump for dedicated infra and networking.
01:28 Lena Ortiz: how much bump? give us ballpark monthly.
01:32 Maya Chen: ballpark numbers in the spreadsheet i'll send: hosted EU is roughly +6% on top of current unit price for geo premium. private VPC reserve is +22-28% depending on commit term and instance sizing, we can optimize with burst pools.
01:46 Raj Kapoor: hmm 22% is significant. can we trade latency for cost by using shared hosted capacity but with a stricter routing to eu nodes?
01:57 Samir Patel: yes you can route by policy. you get ~35-50 ms p95 improvement vs US routing for EU users on hosted eu nodes. private VPC might shave another ~10 ms depending on cross-subnet hops and VPC peering. those are estimates — we'll run a latency baseline during the test window.
02:15 Theo Marsh: timeline question — if we go private VPC, how long until we're live?
02:21 Maya Chen: typical lead is 4-6 weeks for private VPC (provisioning, networking, KMS integration, certs), hosted eu can be activated in 3-5 days.
02:30 Lena Ortiz: we were hoping to align with an upcoming trial start the week of Feb 13. is that plausible?
02:37 Samir Patel: for hosted EU yes easily. private VPC likely tight — might be possible with an expedited path but would require immediate approvals and a short provisioning SOW.
02:50 Raj Kapoor: what's involved on our side for KMS? we want customer-managed keys.
02:56 Maya Chen: we support HSM/KMS integrations. for private VPC you can provide ARN of your KMS or we can set up a BYOK flow. security will need to review key rotation and cross-account access. we can share the security playbook.
03:12 Emily Nguyen: one follow-up — audit logs retention. our compliance needs 7 years of audit logs for certain events. do you store that?
03:21 Jules Ortega: Jules here — we do retain audit logs; retention is configurable per contract and we have long-term archival options. i'll include exact retention tiers in the doc.
03:30 Lena Ortiz: great. can you also include sample retention export format? auditors ask for CSV or JSON schema.
03:36 Jules Ortega: yes will include.
03:40 Raj Kapoor: on the performance side, we need throughput at peak — our morning batch load is around 600 concurrent requests with avg payload 1.2k tokens. how do you size capacity?
03:51 Samir Patel: we size reserved pools by tokens/sec and concurrency. for 600 concurrent and 1.2k tokens avg, we recommend a dedicated pool with autoscale headroom of 30%. with your uplift we can map to X GPUs (we'll put exact mapping in the plan).
04:06 Emily Nguyen: small correction, not all requests are generation — about 40% are embeddings/rerank, so cost profile varies.
04:15 Samir Patel: good note. embeddings are billed per-embedding unit; we can show a blended forecast.
04:20 Lena Ortiz: what about fallbacks? if private VPC capacity saturated, can requests failover to hosted EU?
04:27 Maya Chen: yes, we can set a fallback policy to routed hosted EU or US-hosted depending on your policy. retries and fallbacks are configurable and visible in the Console traces.
04:40 Raj Kapoor: excellent. any SLA delta between hosted and private?
04:45 Maya Chen: SLA is consistent for dedicated pools; private VPC has an SLA that applies to the control plane availability and a slightly different ops window for maintenance. i'll include the exact SLA paragraph in the contract amendment.
04:58 Theo Marsh: procurement — do you need any special redline?
05:02 Maya Chen: standard language for committed capacity change and region addendum. If you want, we can share a templated amendment that lists new committed units, pricing, and termination rights.
05:12 Theo Marsh: yes please.
05:15 Lena Ortiz: on success criteria for the pilot, we'll want: p95 latency under 200ms for triage UI, no failed requests for embeddings during batch windows, and audit/log exports tested.
05:27 Samir Patel: noted. we'll propose test cases and a latency harness.
05:33 Maya Chen: quick note on cost optimization — we can recommend quantization profiles and batching parameters for your mix (embed vs gen) to reduce unit costs without major quality loss. Samir will lead that.
05:45 Raj Kapoor: will the quant recommendations require model changes?
05:48 Samir Patel: no model retrain, mostly quantization at inference layer and batching tweaks, plus cache TTL for prefixes.
05:55 Lena Ortiz: okay good.
06:00 Maya Chen: procurement milestone — Theo, do you have an internal approval date we should target?
06:05 Theo Marsh: aiming to have PO by Jan 20. if we pick hosted EU as interim plan we can move fast and then convert to private VPC later.
06:16 Raj Kapoor: we prefer the private path long-term but will accept hosted as a stop-gap.
06:21 Maya Chen: great. timeline summary: hosted EU activation in ~3 days; private VPC 4-6 weeks. run latency baseline within first week of hosted go-live.
06:33 Lena Ortiz: can we get a dedicated Redwood SE for the first two weeks of the EU pilot?
06:38 Maya Chen: yes Samir and Jules will own the initial week-of-support; we can include a one-week elevated ops window in the amendment.
06:46 Samir Patel: i'll prepare an instrumentation checklist and the latency harness to collect p50/p95/p99.
06:53 Raj Kapoor: also want to run a throughput stress test — shard the 600 concurrent across X clients to emulate real patterns.
06:59 Samir Patel: agreed. we'll provide a stress script and run it with you in a joint session.
07:05 Lena Ortiz: security final question — are there any required attestations for EU data processors?
07:10 Jules Ortega: we provide DPA language and subprocessors list; for private VPC we can include more specific subprocessors and KMS access notes.
07:18 Theo Marsh: good. procurement will review DPA and PO simultaneously.
07:22 Maya Chen: next steps recap: i'll send runbook + pricing; Samir sends test plan and scripts; Jules sends security/RBAC/audit docs; Santella confirms go-live choice and PO timeline.
07:34 Lena Ortiz: can we reconvene after baseline tests? maybe Jan 26 for a short readout?
07:40 Maya Chen: Jan 26 works — i'll pencil it in.
07:44 Raj Kapoor: works for engineering.
07:46 Theo Marsh: works for procurement.
07:48 Maya Chen: perfect. any other loose ends?
07:52 Emily Nguyen: small nit — include an example of billing granularity (daily invoice vs monthly) in the pricing doc.
07:58 Maya Chen: will include.
08:02 Lena Ortiz: ok that's all from me. thanks everyone.
08:06 Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with docs and the action items. bye.
08:10 (meeting end)

Notes on transcript quality: some words garbled by auto-transcript (VPC sometimes becomes V-B-C, KMS as K-M-S etc). We intentionally left filler words and interruptions. The technical sections contain concrete numbers and next steps for procurement and security reviews.
